Title: Assistant   Bakarudin Ishak's Introductory Address at the Forum: Linking United Kingdom & Malaysia
text: Closing Speech by Deputy Governor at Kedah Financial Carnival 2018 Presenter: Datuk Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour / Venue: TH Convention Center, Alor Setar / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: Jan 21, 2018 / I would like to express my deepest appreciation to Yang Berhormat Dato' Wira Othman Bin Aziz, for taking the time with us this evening to complete the closing ceremony of the Kedah Financial Carnival 2018. I would also like to thank the Kedah State Government for their unwavering support in the success of the first Financial Carnival this year and for the first time in the state of Kedah. Kedah was chosen as the third location of the Financial Carnival after Sabah and Sarawak in an effort by Bank Negara Malaysia to expand its financial reach throughout the country. God willing the next location will follow to the East Coast of the homeland. I am very grateful and honoured that the Financial Carnival in the paddy paddy earth has received overwhelming response from all walks of life, especially the B40 group, who come not only from around Kedah but also from far-flung areas such as from Arau in the north, Penang in the middle and the farthest coming from Bagan Datuk, Perak. Well done, I would like to thank you for your willingness to come to this Carnival. According to the statistics given to me, as of 2.00 noon today, more than 25,000 visitors have attended the Financial Carnival. The number of visitors is expected to increase further as it is a public holiday in conjunction with the Sultan of Kedah's Birthday. As can be witnessed by the attendees, the Carnival has brought together so many and various entries under one roof, comprising financial institutions, associations of financial institutions, government agencies and related institutions, which have offered a wide range of financial products and services as well as advisory services to the public. Financial education is an important element in increasing the financial literacy rate among Malaysians. With an increase in knowledge of financial matters, consumers can manage their finances and plan for their future better. Thus, the Financial Carnival is a concerted effort designed to increase the level of financial literacy in all walks of life, from children to adults. To the participants' knowledge, more than 30,000 live advisory services were provided from financial institutions and exhibitors who participated in the carnival. In addition, in line with the objective of the Kedah Financial Carnival targeting the B40 group and micro-entrepreneurs, BNM in collaboration with Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation Sdn. Bhd. (MDEC) has organised eUsahawan and eRezeki workshops and talks that have benefited more than 1700 participants. Of these, almost 200 participants benefited from the workshop session. The latest information we received from MDEC, 30 participants from the eRezeki workshop were able to generate ancillary income, upon completion of the course. Hopefully, all the knowledge that has been learned can be applied and practiced by the participants in order to generate an increase in income and thus improve their standard of living. Recognising the importance of financial education at a young age, Carnival has offered various financial education activities to school students through activities in the children's corner as well as outdoor activities. The continued involvement of several financial institutions such as Prudential Assurance Malaysia, Bank Simpanan Nasional, Bank Rakyat, Alliance Bank and AgroBank, is a noble effort and needs to be emulated by other financial institutions. Such integrated initiatives, will fuel efforts to increase the financial literacy rate among the people to a higher level, in line with the aspirations of the national strategy in increasing the financial literacy rate that will be announced soon. Meanwhile, financial inclusion efforts especially in the ownership of insurance and takaful coverage continued to intensify. To the participants' knowledge, only 4% of households in the low-income group have life insurance or family takaful coverage. Therefore, in line with Bank Negara Malaysia's mandate to develop an inclusive financial system, an affordable protection product was launched in November last year called "Perlindungan Tenang". To date, ten (10) Perlindungan Tenang products have been offered, covering six (6) life insurance products, three (3) family takaful products and one (1) general insurance product. With the availability of this innovative and affordable product offering, it is expected that the percentage of insurance and takaful ownership in the country will continue to increase and achieve our desired targets. With regard to financial crime, statistics show that inquiries about fake calls from the public have increased in recent times. For information, inquiries regarding false calls reported to BNM have increased from 4,316 in 2016 to 7,716 inquiries at the end of 2017. Therefore, I would like to advise the public not to trust and act rashly if they receive such a call. Get more information from the financial institution's official website or contact Bank Negara LINK directly for more information and advice. I would like to congratulate all financial institutions on the initiative undertaken by the coalition of all financial institutions in discharging corporate social responsibility (CSR) through FINCO. FINCO or "Financial Industry Collective Outreach" has organised the inaugural Life Aspiration Talk series held at this Carnival. It is a continuation of the activities carried out in raising the aspirations for the young, especially to the less fortunate and under-exposure, so that they are eager to continue to rise and succeed in their lives. Continue this noble endeavour and jointly contribute to the development of human capital to support the well-being of the community and the development of the country. In line with the rapid development of digital technology, digital initiatives will continue to be introduced. For example, the launch of eCCRIS and MyDebit Corporate Card are among the digital initiatives that will continue to be implemented and supported. Aspiration to transform the payment system in the country into an electronic payment system will increase efficiency in the economy as well as drive the transition to a high-income and value-added economy. This effort is vital to ensure that the financial sector continues to grow and be inclusive in meeting the future needs of Malaysians. In addition, Bank Negara Malaysia has also taken the opportunity from the Carnival to interact with Carnival visitors to deepen the aspirations of Malaysians on the role of the financial sector for the next 30 years. The aspirations collected will be translated in the success of the National Transformation 2050 (TN50). More than 1,050 aspirations have been received from visitors who are generally focused on three main aspects. First, they hope that by 2050, financial transactions will be made cashless. Second, they hope that by 2050, the level of financial literacy among Malaysians will rise to a high level. In this regard, visitors also say that financial institutions should offer suitable products to increase their retirement savings. In the third aspiration, they think social impact finance is important for the future and access to it needs to be expanded to become more universal. On behalf of Bank Negara Malaysia, I would like to thank you for the sharing that has been given to us. Before I end this speech, I would once again like to thank the Deputy Minister of Finance I, the Kedah State Government and the state government agencies for all the cooperation given in ensuring the smooth running of the Carnival. My heartfelt congratulations and thanks also to the financial institutions as well as all parties involved and those who participated in sponsoring various programmes and incentives throughout the Carnival. Finally, I believe that this joint venture will encourage stronger and more comprehensive cooperation between various parties in the future in order to make Malaysia a developed nation in all aspects.

Title: Speech by the  at the Launching Ceremony of the Funding Advisory Service
text: Speech by Assistant Governor at the Opening Ceremony of the Print Art Exhibition: Art of All Times Presenter: Mr. Abu Hassan Alshari Yahaya / Venue: Sasana Kijang, Kuala Lumpur / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: 28 August 2018 / Thank You Alhamdulillah for today we can come together in completing the Opening Ceremony of the Exhibition of Print Art: Art of All Time. My deepest appreciation goes to all the artists, collectors, staff of the Bank Negara Malaysia Museum and Art Gallery who worked hard to make this exhibition a reality. I would also like to express my gratitude to the audience for taking the time to increase the excitement of our occasion today. ART IN GENERAL AND BANK NEGARA MALAYSIA The most frequently asked question is, what is the relationship between Bank Negara Malaysia and art? What is in the art of encouraging Bank Negara Malaysia to play an active and profound role. At first glance, Art and Banking may not show a clear and natural relevance. However, art actually has a close relationship in the development of the nation, civilization as well as the progress of the nation. The transition of art is a reflection of the change of the country and its inhabitants in all aspects; especially social, political and economic civilizations. The process of development and maturity of local art is especially noticeable and it will continue. This can be witnessed through: 1. Such a wide selection of art subjects, from scenes, figures and subsequently abstracts; 2. The variety of innovating media, from watercolors, oil paints, acrylic paints, batik to mixed media; And 3. The delivery of an increasingly vocal message from a picture that ranges locally to a more global issue. This is not only a process of physical modernization but also a clear explanation, it is also a testament to the process of changing thoughts and expressions that give a picture of the past, the present, but also the future to share. PRINT ART: ART THROUGHOUT THE AGES All of them will be aware of Bank Negara Malaysia's role in expanding the financial inclusion. It is an important mandate of the Bank so that all levels of society can achieve economic progress as well as gain access to financial services and financial information. Similarly in the field of art, Bank Negara Malaysia has always been committed to empowering art inclusion by providing access to the arts to its performers, observers and the community at large. Implemented through the Bank Negara Malaysia Museum and Art Gallery, this effort is part of our social responsibility to enrich and highlight the art and culture of the nation's heritage. It started with the collection of artworks as early as the 1960s followed by exhibitions and art programmes that have intensified over the past 4 decades to date. If previously we were often exposed to more 'mainstream' artworks such as oil paint paintings, watercolors and acrylic. Now, it's time for us to highlight the Art of Print: The Art of All Time. From the point of view of the naked eye, many see this print artwork as not much different from the paintwork. It's not accurate. If many people like to work directly on sheets of paper and canvas, art artists play with materials of an 'industrial' nature such as wooden blocks, stones and metal sheets. The process of producing artistic imagery-imagery is accompanied by the use of sharp, acid and now, thermal tools. The art of print is not limited to painting and painting but they also cut, sculpt, pry, press and sometimes step on to produce works. All this sounds very crunchy and rugged. The techniques of printed art such as wood cut, sleigh, saring silk and pirography require not only a strong kudrat but also a strong patience in the intensive process of experimentation. In championing this identity towards the art of print, not many were strong enough and retreated and moved on to a more commercial field of fine arts. However, today, through this exhibition, it has been proven that many artists continue to be faithful to the art of print. And more proudly, the challenge of this struggle is confirmed by young artists with the application of techniques and the production of increasingly bold works. The question arises  Why do these artists choose to work in such a complicated way? The key words are 'challenge' and 'satisfaction'. The challenge in the production of this print artwork is so dynamic that the technique is constantly evolving. These artists always want to make sure what can be produced in a comparable print work or preferably beyond a paintwork. However, the process is different and of course, the challenges multiply. It has been proven that this art presents an incredible physical challenge to them, they also consider this art to be a 'healthy mind challenge' where the potential of the artist's mind is always optimized. As for the print artwork, the color application process is not something so spontaneous and as simple as brush strokes. The colouring process also requires a detailed study and strategy  which parts need to be posed, submerged, left empty or coloured? It is these challenges that are their hardcore driving force in this field. The artistic value of print art extends beyond aesthetic value. It has a character full of detail, both physically and mentally  this is the satisfaction that its artists are looking for. PRINT ART AND BANKNOTE PRINT In addition to celebrating artists and their works, the exhibition also highlights the general confusion between printing and print art. Although the concept is the same, however, the technique is somewhat different. What is interesting is that print is not a foreign matter for Bank Negara Malaysia. It began when Bank Negara Malaysia issued its first currency on 12 June 1967. The art of printing and printing banknotes has a lot in common. Among the similarities that certainly interest us all is in terms of its artistic effect. Both the art of printing and printing banknotes apply the intaglio technique. Who would have thought this intaglio technique serves as one of the security features of banknotes so that it is difficult to replicate or fake. If anyone is still wondering how this texture is applied to the banknote, I invite you all to remove any banknotes from your wallet and swipe your finger on the first portrait of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong. The embossed effect is the intaglio effect. COVER This exhibition is a tribute to the spirit of the 29 artists as well as the uniqueness of their works. It is a manifestation of the artist's artistic, meticulousness, determination and patience. Congratulations to the artists for their hard work in preserving the future of print art. Hopefully, it will inspire other artists in Malaysia. The highest appreciation is directed to the entire family of this exhibition; The artists involved and art collectors for their unwavering cooperation and support in ensuring that this art appreciation initiative continues to be applied to all walks of life. Again, thank you also to all of you for coming with us at the launch of this exhibition which took place from 25 August to 25 November 2018. We hope that you will not only be able to observe the beauty and subtlety of the artworks on display as well as appreciate the direct and indirect messages on display but will also invigorate the spirit of art around you. Finally, I would like to unveil the quote of the country's artist, Syed Ahmad Jamal: "The role of the artist  a social one" - Here, he emphasizes that the role of artists does not cease to be on the work alone, but rather includes their relationships and interactions with the public. This is our hope, that this exhibition will be a link between all of us. Thank you, wabillahi taufik wal hidayah, wassalamualaikum w.b.t. and in conjunction with the country's 61 years of independence, Love My Malaysia. 0

Title: Minister of Finance's Speech at the Seventh Malaysian Insurance Industry Annual Dinner 1999
text: Welcome Speech by the Governor at the Launching Ceremony of the Affordable Home Fund and My Home Portal Presenter: Datuk Nor Shamsiah Mohd Yunus / Venue: Sasana Kijang, Kuala Lumpur / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: 29 Jan 2019 / On behalf of Bank Negara Malaysia, I welcome the presence of the Honorable Minister of Finance, and the Honorable Minister of Housing and Local Government, to the Launching Ceremony of the Affordable Home Fund, and the Rumahku Portal. We are pleased to have the opportunity to take the time to complete the launch of the Affordable Home Fund and My Home Portal. Bank Negara Malaysia and the Credit Counseling and Management Agency (AKPK), as co-organisers, would also like to take this opportunity to express their gratitude for the support and cooperation of the financial institutions involved in the success of the Affordable Home Fund and Rumahku Portal initiative. Owning a home involves a large investment or financial commitment. Prospective homebuyers should be responsible for assessing their affordability level, to meet financial commitments related to the cost of owning a home, including loan repayments and other related expenses. Bank Negara Malaysia would like to emphasise the importance of adopting a prudent financial management culture as financially literate individuals will be able to make better financial decisions. They will be more prudent in planning their financial needs, free from the shackles of excessive debt and able to adequately prepare for retirement life. In fact, they may be able to achieve financial independence. Various efforts are being taken to foster a culture of prudent financial management starting from a young age. Bank Negara Malaysia's 2018 survey showed a low level of financial literacy among the people, including knowledge in financial issues, as well as behaviour and attitudes regarding financial management. Among the weaknesses identified include a large number of people who cannot afford unexpected expenses, with 52% admitting to having difficulty raising RM1,000 in the event of an emergency. Moreover, only 24% of citizens are confident of fulfilling financial obligations for at least three months in case of loss of income. Although there are improvements when compared to the same study in 2015, overall there are still many financial capability gaps that need to be addressed. Therefore, Bank Negara Malaysia together with the Financial Education Network is developing a national financial literacy strategy aimed at improving the level of financial literacy as well as fostering prudent financial behaviour and attitude. In this regard, in an effort to help the target segment make prudent financial decisions in owning this first home, the Credit Counseling and Management Agency (AKPK) has provided a simple and convenient online financial education module on the Rumahku Portal. This effort is in line with AKPK's role in providing financial education, counselling and financial advice as well as offering credit management programmes to individuals who have trouble repaying loans. The Rumahku portal helps prospective borrowers to understand and manage their finances effectively through a simple and simple self-assessment. Prospective borrowers will get a clear picture of the financial commitments they will face after buying a house and getting a loan. The target group should be aware that owning a home through financing must be based on the ability to repay the financing in full. Since its launch earlier this year, a total of 1037 have completed the financial education programme through the Rumahku Portal. Of these, a total of 265 voluntarily did not pursue the intention of applying for housing financing when they realised they did not have sufficient financial capacity at this time. The Affordable Home Fund, with an allocation of RM1 billion, will help homebuyers from low-income groups across the country fund their first home purchase. The Fund is expected to enhance the target segment's ability to own a first home with a low financing rate of 3.5% per annum. This incentive is estimated to contribute to a lower monthly instalment of 23% compared to the existing financing scheme. The fund is offered for two years from 2 January 2019 through five financial institutions participating in the scheme. However, the Affordable Home Fund with low financing rates should be seen as a temporary facility, for a limited period and prudently implemented. To ensure that home financing continues to be sustainable, the home financing rate needs to reflect the actual risk costs faced by the financial institution taking into account the cost of funds, administrative costs, and the liquidity and credit risk of the loan. Addressing the issue of affordable housing is a shared responsibility so that the ongoing gap between house prices and the affordability of owning a home can be reduced. Bank Negara Malaysia and its financial institutions remain committed to providing transformative financial services to enable all walks of life to save, invest and borrow productively and improve their quality of life. Meanwhile, buyers need to have sufficient savings and the ability to pay their loans throughout the loan tenure to ensure home ownership. Prospective homebuyers are also advised to take practical steps in giving priority to the main commitment of living expenses so that the increase in debt through home financing does not further burden their financial position. The issue of affordable home ownership requires a holistic solution with the involvement of all parties involved in order to be resolved in a shorter period of time. Housing developers and local authorities also need to be prepared to jointly realize this agenda. The centralisation of affordable housing initiatives through one entity and the creation of an integrated housing database should be hastened. This integrated database is important in addressing the issue of houses offered by developers that do not match the level of affordability of the local people. Efforts to reduce construction costs by developers should also be taken to ensure that house prices can be reduced to more affordable levels. In addition, economic policies that will promote employment and income growth of the people are also important in improving their socio-economic and financial position to own a home. Once again, on behalf of Bank Negara Malaysia and AKPK would like to express my deepest appreciation to Yang Berhormat Tuan Lim Guan Eng, Minister of Finance and Yang Berhormat Puan Hajjah Zuraida binti Kamaruddin, Minister of Housing and Local Government for their support in launching the Affordable Home Fund and Rumahku Portal. To the attendees, thank you again for being present at this event and hopefully this initiative can be implemented well and successfully and can be benefited by the targeted groups. Thank you.

Title: Speech at the Malaysian Insurance Industry Dinner
text: Print Keynote address by the Assistant Governor at Muzakarah Cendekiawan Shariah Nusantara 13th Presenter: Aznan bin Abdul Aziz / Venue: The Rizqun International Hotel, Gadong, Brunei Darussalam / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: 23 Jul 2019 / Alhamdulillah, my highest gratitude goes to Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala, for with His grace, we are met in the Thirteenth Muzakarah Cendekiawan Shariah Nusantara (13th) this year. I would also like to express my appreciation to ISRA as the organizer of today's invitation. Indeed, the Muzakarah organization over the past decade has given us the space and opportunity to jointly explore the Islamic financial system at the archipelago level. Various ideas and innovations have been triggered through intellectual thinking and discussion. This was also followed by measures to tap into the potential and drive Islamic financial performance. Empowerment of the financial sector towards sustainable development If we exemplify the philosophy of Shariah more deeply, the matter of preserving universal prosperity and achieving sustainability of life, is an important foundation in the socio-economic development of the people as a whole. In this regard, Islam has outlined the principles of justice, equality and transparency as a clear guide in muamalat and community activities. In fact, this philosophy has been universally accepted by the global financial community as a specific agenda. For example, the principles of sustainability have been reflected into the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals ("Sustainable Development Goals") or SDGs, which focus on equitable socio-economic development as well as good environmental preservation. These principles have been an important back-up in the formulation of financial products and services solutions globally. Nevertheless, the uniqueness of Shariah philosophy over global practice is that Shariah philosophy is based on Shariah adherence. If we reflect on the Islamic financial landscape today, it has undergone a transformation that goes beyond imagination. Integration with global markets through cross-border trading driven by the digital revolution has changed the pattern and pace of Islamic financial transactions. Various innovations of new products and services have been introduced and offered to meet the needs of increasingly sophisticated customers. However, socio-economic problems are intensifying. Among them, the wealth gap is becoming more pronounced every year. Based on the OXFAM Report discussed at the World Economic Forum 2019 held in Davos, a total of 3.8 billion hardcore poor individuals have experienced an 11 percent decline in wealth in 2018[2]. This raises the question, "to what extent have the core values of Shariah been applied in the supply of Islamic financial products in addressing current socio-economic issues?" There is no doubt that there are initiatives to apply these values into the framework of Islamic monetary policy. For example, in Malaysia, the introduction of the Value-Based Mediation Framework ("Value-based Intermediation Framework")[3] or VBI in 2018 acts as a catalyst for the transformation of sustainability practices in the Islamic financial sector. In particular, the VBI framework plays an important role in the coordination between the values, practices and operations of Islamic financial institutions towards targeting the positive impact not only on consumers of financial products and services, but also on the environment through the creation of financial solutions that align with the sustainability agenda. In this regard, efforts to achieve this sustainability goal should be displayed as a serious commitment in bridging the socio-economic prosperity gap, especially among Muslim countries. Wide investment gap between developing countries in sustainability project financing[4] a clear signal that there is an urgent need for the Islamic finance industry to play its role more aggressively. Therefore, towards realising this aspiration, the Shariah scholars community has an important role to play in jointly implementing a paradigm shift in formulating progressive initiatives and being able to change initiatives with three main elements: First: The application of social instruments into financial products to generate a more significant impact; Second: Empowerment of inter-sector collaboration in enhancing synergies and outcomes in social initiatives; and Third: Technology integration for more comprehensive and efficient access. The application of social instruments into financial products to generate a more significant impact In order to ensure progressive socio-economic development, the implementation of zakat, waqf and sadaqah should not be limited to the provision of basic necessities and self-sufficiency alone. Often, it is channeled specifically for religious purposes such as building mosques and madrasahs. On the other hand, this social financial instrument should also be targeted for the purpose of helping the poor to achieve self-reliance in the long run. This can be achieved if the authorities and financial institutions work together to channel this social financial fund as a source of business capital assistance equipped with training services, advice and technical and management expertise. Such initiatives can help the poor and the poor out of the minimum affordability rate limit (kifayah limit). For example, in Indonesia, for every 100 zakat recipients as economic capital, 17% have successfully exited asnaf status in less than 5 years. This is an impressive achievement. In view of this, there is still a lot of effort that can be intensified to bridge the socio-economic gap of the regional community. Therefore, Islamic financial institutions need to come up with more innovative and inclusive financial solutions and products through the application of social financial instruments into the offering of products and services by Islamic financial institutions. This initiative makes the management and use of social instrument facilities more effective and comprehensive. In Malaysia, for example, the collaboration between six (6) Islamic banking institutions and the State Islamic Religious Council enables Islamic banking institutions to offer fundraising and distribution facilities for their customers through the MyWakaf digital platform, thus making it easier for the public to participate.[5] This platform not only facilitates waqf activities, but has also fostered a culture of transparency through the disclosure of detailed information on the use of waqf funds collected. In 2018, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Berhad as one of the banking institutions in the strategic partnership reported a waqf fundraising of RM20 million.[6] In line with the principles applied in Shariah regarding trust in administration, the party mandated to lead the social administration institution must also emphasize the implementation of good governance with integrity and accountability. History has proven that through the wisdom of Caliph Umar bin Abdul Aziz in administering the affairs of baitul mal and the treasury of the country, he has successfully launched financial affairs through a structured and efficient collection and distribution of zakat and waqf funds, thus creating well-being in the community until there is no more poor in the era.[7]. This Sirah should be used as a tauladan in shaping a culture of good governance among the administrative institutions of zakat and waqf as well as Islamic financial institutions through compliance with the principles of disclosure (disclosure) and transparency (transparency) to increase the confidence of the public, especially in the management and distribution of zakat and waqf funds. An example that can be seen is the ISO 9001 accreditation of the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore[8] obtained from Singapore Quality Institute. The accreditation focuses on the disclosure of clear, accurate and relevant information for public information, in addition to recognizing the quality of management of funds and waqf property. This should be emphasized by zakat management bodies and religious councils. The quality of governance can also be enhanced through strategic cooperation with financial institutions due to the existing corporate governance rules that must be complied with by financial institutions in general. Such disclosures are not only aimed at informing about the social financial activities that have been carried out, but also to create awareness to the community on the positive impact on the socio-economic development that they have generated through the contribution of zakat, waqf and sadaqah. Now, the mobilization of digital information is moving rapidly. To ensure widespread access to information, disclosure through social media and websites plays an important role in ensuring more effective communication. Thus, the institutions of administration of zakat and waqf need to hone the efficiency of the use of social media to channel accurate and relevant information to the general public. Empowerment of inter-sectoral collaboration in increasing synergies and outcomes in social initiatives The saying goes: "Round the water because of the sewer, round man because of the consensus." In an increasingly challenging global economic environment, the cooperation of various sectors in the management of zakat, waqf and sadaqah is critical. This can ensure progressive and inclusive socio-economic development. Through such collaboration, various sectors have the opportunity to mobilize and leverage their respective expertise in the distribution of social funds and formulate sustainable and effective strategies in order to address socio-economic problems as well as to pioneer the potential of these instruments to the optimum level. Such collaborations can bear fruit on a larger scale. There are many initiatives that I can share through this kind of collaboration. Among them is the mobile clinic initiative, the result of a collaboration between Bank Muamalat Malaysia Berhad, Perbadanan Wakaf Selangor and two hospitals in providing access to medicine through a vehicle modified into a mobile clinic. This clinic's services are not only focused on the target group, but also target disaster areas that require medical and health focus. Since its introduction, this mobile clinic has served over 9,000 patients in its various service branches covering 3 areas in Selangor and Kelantan[9]. The collaboration between the United Nations Development Programme and the Directorate General of New and Renewable Energy and Energy Conservation, Indonesia (DJEBTKE), supported by Badan Amil Zakat Indonesia (BAZNAS) and Bank Jambi is also exemplary. In 2018, this collaboration has successfully launched a renewable energy preparation project using zakat funds to provide electricity to the residents in Jambi district, Indonesia. About 803 houses involving 4,500 residents in Jambi district have enjoyed electricity facilities that will catalyse the economic sustainability, education and health of the locals.[10]This initiative demonstrates the synergistic capabilities of various sectors in producing positive impacts on sustainability goals. Through the sharing of these experiences from countries, such as on the forum field today, I believe it will spark new ideas in building social initiatives that will have a greater and more meaningful impact. Therefore, regional cooperation and synergies should be intensified in empowering social financial instruments for mutual benefit. Technology integration for more comprehensive and efficient access The evolution of technology has now changed the business environment to become more dynamic. The Islamic finance industry is certainly no exception to the technological revolution that challenges the current norms of Islamic finance practices. In enhancing the institutional's ability towards more comprehensive and efficient access, the exploration of innovative solutions using technology is a step forward that needs to be agile. For example, in Malaysia, rivals from 93 fintech companies[11] offering Islamic financial services should not be considered as a deterrent from staying viable. In fact, it should be seen as a collaborative opportunity for technological integration to create more futuristic solutions. This potential is also not a foreign subject in the context of the provision of social financial solutions. If we review the initiative of one of the fintech companies, Finterra, a system using blockchain technology named as Waqf Chain has been developed. It will not only speed up the process of raising waqf funds for the development of a waqf project, but also ensure transparency in its management. The integration of this technology also, if explored to an optimal level, is able to provide solutions to the socio-economic issues underlying the problem of access gap to basic services. For example, in an effort to treat the economic disparity in Indonesia, the potential for QR code-based digital payments has been explored to catalyze financial inclusion efforts that cover all segments of society.[12]. This initiative is a synergy of joint ventures between the Indonesian government, financial institutions, as well as fintech companies. In boosting the integration of this technology into the creation of solutions based on Islamic financial instruments, the role of Shariah scholars must be strengthened in enhancing the efficiency of technology mastery so that these solutions can achieve the desired sustainability goals. Thus, the integration of technology in the implementation of social financial instruments will not only ensure a more efficient and orderly implementation, but also contribute in strengthening Islamic finance in the future. Conclusion As we are facing a dynamic and challenging financial sector, the implementation of social financial solutions needs to be more elastic and creative. As Shariah scholars, regulators, practitioners of the Islamic financial industry and individuals as a whole, we should always be aware and ready to adapt and innovate to remain relevant in the future. In order to realise our aspirations and implement this inspiration, our role is very important in educating the community that the Islamic finance industry is not merely to maximise profits. In fact, it also aims to improve socio-economic development and address the crisis that is engulfing the world today through financial instruments that are in line with Shariah needs. Therefore, more effective synergies require the inclusion of the role of all parties to carry out the trust with integrity and ethics and always work together to plan and achieve the targets that have been set. Finally, I pray and hope that the muzakarah this time can run smoothly and achieve the targeted objectives. Thank you, Wabillahi taufik wal hidayah. Title: Keynote Address at the UNDP Islamic Finance International Conference
text: Speech by the Governor at the Launching Ceremony of the Funding Advisory Service Presenter: Datuk Nor Shamsiah Mohd Yunus / Venue: Sasana Kijang, Kuala Lumpur / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: 21 August 2019 / On behalf of Bank Negara Malaysia, I welcome the attendance to the Launching Ceremony of the Financing Advisory Service. We would also like to thank you for the support and cooperation of the financial institutions in making this initiative a success. The financial sector continues to play an important role in supporting small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and households especially in the face of a challenging financial and economic environment. Funding by the financial sector, as a whole, is consistent with the current economic growth rate of 4.9% in the second quarter of 2019. Net financing in the second quarter of 2019 expanded by 5.6% on an annual basis. The constant issuance of loans to all segments of the economy continues to support the economic activities of the country. SMEs are an important business segment to financial institutions, accounting for 87% of the total business customer accounts. SMEs continued to receive financing support and this is evidenced by higher financing withdrawals for the first half of 2019 of RM152 billion compared to RM149 billion for the first half of 2018. In addition, financial institutions continued to support home ownership, with the approval of new housing loans worth RM78.5 billion for the first six months of the year, benefiting over 180,000 borrowers. What is notable is the affordability of housing financing repayments which is still a major challenge for prospective homeowners. A sustainable and sound financial system continues to be the main strength of the Malaysian economy. This enables financial institutions to play a role in supporting the SME and household segments through the provision of financing at various phases of the business. The stable loan approval rate proves that financial institutions continue to provide financing to viable businesses and eligible borrowers, even in a challenging economic environment. It catalyzes financial institutions to be more proactive, dynamic and innovative in providing financial services especially to assist customers affected by the current economic situation. This includes assisting customers to improve their eligibility for financing through credit guarantees by CGC and Cagamas as well as services available by credit bureaus. Advisory services by financial institutions, CGC and AKPK as well as various Government agencies can also help businesses and individuals better manage their credit facilities. As a leading financial services provider, banking institutions must continue to play a role in identifying potential, guiding and supporting borrowers to be more viable. Owning a business or a home, involves large investments or financial commitments. Undoubtedly, the sustainable credit market supports the country's economic activities and plays a role in complementing the infrastructure and ecosystem of SMEs or households. However, the provision of loans or financing should be carried out prudently and responsibly to ensure that borrowers do not borrow beyond their means so as to result in a business or an individual facing difficulties and financial burdens in the future. SMEs and prospective borrowers should be responsible for assessing their level of capabilities, to meet financial commitments. For example, since the launch of the Rumahku Portal earlier this year, a total of 12,223 individuals have completed their financial education programmes. Of these, a total of 1,628 voluntarily did not pursue the intention of applying for housing financing when they realised they did not have sufficient financial capabilities and buffers at this time. The initiatives undertaken by Bank Negara Malaysia to encourage responsible financing remain relevant and have contributed to the stability of the financial sector as well as ensuring that the end goal of home ownership is achieved. To ensure that business and housing financing applicants continue to receive advice and assistance, Bank Negara Malaysia, in collaboration with CGC, AKPK and financial institutions will offer one-stop advisory services to financing applicants who are unsuccessful in obtaining loans by setting up a "Financing Advisory Service". This one-stop centre offers advice, ease and steps that can be taken to improve eligibility for financing applications as well as to open up wider and more suitable alternative financing options. In particular, the Financing Advisory Service assists SME financing applicants and homebuyers through the following 3 steps: 1. First, help applicants understand the factors in which their application is rejected. Although financial institutions need to state the reasons for the application being rejected, the Funding Advisory Service will assist to provide further evidence such as an assessment of the ability to repay the financing; 2. secondly, assist applicants in obtaining advice on ways to improve eligibility for future financing, such as keeping complete financial management records; And 3. thirdly, help the applicant get an alternative solution. For viable SMEs, CGC will refer them to alternative sources of financing. As for homebuyers, AKPK will refer applicants to alternative solutions including e-rezeki to improve eligibility, financial education modules at the Rumahku Portal and credit management programmes to enhance and provide prospective borrowers with good credit management knowledge. The Funding Advisory Service initiative is expected to increase the awareness and credibility of financial users by bridging the asymmetrical information gap between consumers and financial institutions. This initiative also complements the efforts taken by Bank Negara Malaysia to promote a strong, progressive and inclusive financial sector. Despite the different target segments, Bank Negara Malaysia would like to emphasise the importance of financial institutions, CGC and AKPK working together, especially in empowering the Financing Advisory Service as a 'one-stop centre' in the future. Various measures have been taken in the effort to assist the business sector as well as households. To support the development of SMEs, Bank Negara Malaysia has spearheaded the building of a holistic financing ecosystem to increase access to financing while promoting a strong credit culture. Among the initiatives introduced by Bank Negara Malaysia include the Micro Financing Scheme, the Credit Guarantee Scheme by CGC, the BNM Fund for SMEs amounting to RM9.1 billion, two years of flexibility on the restructuring and rescheduling of SME financing and the Small Loan Settlement Scheme for viable SMEs. Financial institutions are urged to remain proactive in carrying out the restructuring and rescheduling of financing. For homebuyers, the RM1 billion special fund allocation launched in early January this year will help homebuyers from the low-income group finance the purchase of a first home. In addition to assisting the target group in owning their first home, Bank Negara Malaysia is pleased to inform the following criteria and characteristics of the Affordable Home Fund: 1. first, increase the eligibility of applicants by Malaysian citizens with a maximum monthly household income from RM2,300 to a maximum income of B40 which is currently at RM4,360; And 2. Second, increasing the maximum price limit of eligible houses to be funded from RM150,000 to RM300,000, in line with the definition of affordable housing price in the National Affordable Housing Policy. Once again, on behalf of Bank Negara Malaysia, I would like to express my deepest appreciation to AKPK, CGC and the financial institutions for their support in launching this Financing Advisory Service. To the attendees, thank you again for being willing to attend this event and hopefully this initiative can be implemented well and successfully and can be used by the targeted groups. You are also welcome to visit the exhibition space outside this hall provided by AKPK and CGC to understand more about the Financing Advisory Services as well as sales stalls by SMEs. With the phrase Bismillah-hirRahman-niRahim I hereby officiate this Financing Advisory Service. Ikuti Kami Notis Perundangan Terma Penggunaan Penafian Dasar Privasi & Kuki

text: Speech by Assistant Governor at the Opening Ceremony of the LA Financial Coordination Exhibition Presenter: Mr. Abu Hassan Alshari Yahaya / Venue: Terengganu State Museum, Terengganu, Malaysia / Language: English / Speech/Interview Date: 25 August 2019 / In terms of its background, the LATerasi Kewangan Exhibition was launched at Bank Negara Malaysia Museum and Art Gallery, Kuala Lumpur in 2015. It is an exhibition of caricatures of Datuk Lat's own work published in 14 series of Bank Negara Malaysia's Wang Saku Book from 1999 to 2012. It aims to inculcate the habit of managing money prudently from a young age. With the overwhelming response and feedback, the exhibition was later made as a 'moving exhibition' across the country. This financial adventure began on a small scale for the first time at the Paddy Museum, Kedah during International Museum Day 2016. It went on to the Penang State Museum in the same year and to the Darul Ridzuan Museum, Perak in 2018. And now the time has come, we bring the compilation of this caricature of the Wang Saku Book to Terengganu, the east coast state chosen as the location of the LaTerasi Kewangan Exhibition. I believe the Financial Coordination Exhibition at the Terengganu State Museum will also receive encouraging response especially from fans and followers of Datuk Lat's works. Financial education is an important thing to empower Malaysians with the necessary knowledge and skills to enhance their well-being. Increasing financial knowledge allows people to manage their financial affairs and plan their future more wisely. Thus, Buku Wang Saku is one of the efforts to increase the level of financial literacy starting from childhood. It aims to help students track expenses and guide them to manage pocket money effectively. Bank Negara Malaysia is very pleased that Datuk Lat has been able to make a strong and meaningful commitment in translating sometimes elusive topics into more interesting and understandable for school students. As a result, since 1999, approximately 15.5 million copies of the Wang Saku Book have been distributed to more than 10,000 schools nationwide to provide exposure on financial affairs to school students. The caricatures of Datuk Lat's sketches through Buku Wang Saku have attracted the attention of students, teachers and parents, where the book is widely used as a tool to track their finances, foster savings habits and thus promote prudent financial management. His work has touched on various aspects of financial management such as savings; what is the difference between needs and wants; avoid waste and many others that are conveyed through creative and entertaining visuals. These caricatures are infused with interesting essences that give a real-life picture of the diversity of society in Malaysia in terms of race, culture and tradition. In addition, his work also has a positive impact in promoting social harmony and noble values. Many Malaysians grew up with his work that has touched on various aspects of life as well as giving us a picture of the social environment as well as the economic and political developments in the country. Among the characters featured in the Wang Saku Book include the characters in the Kampung Boy cartoon series Mat, the mischievous and Mrs. Hiew, who is known as a fierce character. In this exhibition, elements of the state of Terengganu are also applied to bring it closer to the local visitors. Bank Negara Malaysia plays an active role in emphasising financial education for school students and children from early age to adults so that they can make smarter financial decisions. Among the initiatives introduced are: i. First, the Advisory and Services Information Site (BNMLINK) which provides various channels for the public to obtain financial services information and financial advisory services. This directly increases the level of financial literacy. ii. Second, a financial education programme for civil servants where in 2018, Bank Negara Malaysia has implemented 29 interaction programmes on awareness of prudent financial management that benefited 2,354 civil servants from various ministries and government agencies throughout Malaysia as well as interaction through 'Train-theTrainer' involving 7,914 civil servants through 180 standalone programmes organised. iii. Third, the Financial Carnival is organized at the national and state levels to reach out to the people through a financial inclusion programme that brings together so many and various entries under one roof, comprising financial institutions, associations of financial institutions, as well as government and private agencies. The carnival fosters awareness on banking, insurance and takaful products and services, as well as providing updates on financial fraud issues as well as how to recognize the ringgit currency and its security features. The national level started at PWTC, Kuala Lumpur in January 2017, then to Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, Kuching, Sarawak and flew back to the north of Alor Setar peninsula, Kedah in January 2018. Most recently, in April this year, at the TH Hotel and Convention Centre, the national financial carnival was held in the state of Terengganu itself. While at the district level, in the last year and this year, we have been to several districts such as Jerantut, Labuan, Taiping, Miri and Melaka Tengah. The national and district carnival has attracted more than 150,000 visitors. The National Financial Literacy Strategy was just launched by YAB Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad on 23 July 2019. This strategy was developed by the Financial Education Network (FENetwork), an inter-agency group led by Bank Negara Malaysia and the Securities Commission Malaysia (SSM) together with its founding members comprising representatives from the Ministry of Education Malaysia (MOE), Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM), Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Credit Counseling and Management Agency (AKPK) and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB). This National Strategy sets out priorities and action plans to improve the financial wellbeing of Malaysians. Joint efforts with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to foster good financial values from a young age have recorded the progressive integration of financial education into the school curriculum to Form Two. The integration is expected to be implemented for all levels of primary and secondary schools by 2021. In addition to financial education in schools, Bank Negara Malaysia also uses various channels and platforms to promote financial awareness and education for the public on an ongoing basis. A total of 1,700 learning sessions on personal financial management were conducted by the Credit Counseling and Management Agency (AKPK) nationwide which reached over 1.6 million people during 2018. In the state of Terengganu, more than 116 thousand people have received financial counseling while more than 26 thousand people have entered the debt management program to help them settle their debts in an orderly manner. The LATerasi Kewangan exhibition honours Datuk Lat's continued legacy for his significant contribution to the country including his efforts in supporting us to improve our financial management skills and enrich the Malaysian arts. I would like to thank Datuk Lat for his service over the years. I would like to thank Yang Amat Berhormat Dato' Seri Dr. Ahmad Samsuri bin Mokhtar, the Menteri Besar of Terengganu for being willing to attend the opening of this exhibition in Kuala Terengganu. Thank you to the Terengganu State Museum Board for their cooperation and support in ensuring that this exhibition is planned and implemented successfully. And thank you also to all of you for being able to be with us in the launch of this LaTerasi Kewangan exhibition which will run until February 2020 at the Terengganu State Museum. I believe all of you will be comforted by Datuk Lat's creative paintings while appreciating the message he wants to convey.
